attribution.note: Marcus's own current assessment in the 'Two years later' paragraph. It is not a quote of his earlier argument.

semantics.note: Keeps the 'not 5 specifically' exclusion and both parts: costly to run, and a growing issue. Reading it as about OpenAI fits the paragraph.

contract.note: No measure is named, so the plain reading (expensive to serve, inference cost a growing burden, e.g. margin pressure) is ordinary and fair. Using 2025 through the post date is a reasonable window.

evidence.note: Press report of internal figures: inference cost quadrupled in 2025. Much of that was demand-driven, but it shows a large and growing running cost.
Adjusted gross margin fell from 40% to 33% in 2025, tied to inference costs. This fits cost being a growing issue.
Measures customer billed cost for GPT-5.5 against 5.4, not OpenAI's serving cost. Context only.

reviews.rationale: Reported inference costs quadrupled and margins fell in 2025. Both were available before the post and meet the support condition. Older-tier price cuts (o3) are noted, but they don't show the latest models are cheap to run or that margins improved. Figures are press estimates, not audited.

attribution.note: Marcus's own current words, written as an update on his earlier argument.

semantics.note: Faithful to both parts. 'Had to' carries an implied element of competitive necessity, which the contract keeps.

contract.note: An informed reader would take 'had to cut prices' to mean cuts driven by competition. Requiring that link is ordinary and fair. 'Caught up' as broad parity is also fair.

evidence.note: Stanford AI Index, March 2026 Arena: top four within 25 points, with OpenAI fourth. Supports convergence.
OpenAI changelog, June 2025: o3 price cut for an existing model. A valid dated pricing record. It is silent on the cause.
OpenAI credits inference optimisation for the cut. That does not rule out competitive pressure, but it gives no support for it.

reviews.rationale: The evidence supports that competitors caught up and that OpenAI actually cut prices. The contract's support condition also needs credible evidence that competition drove the cuts. The packet has none, and the only stated reason is efficiency. The contract says missing evidence does not contradict, so the full claim stays unsettled.
